source.title: Generalized Cross Entropy Loss for Training Deep Neural Networks with Noisy Labels

record.tranche_reason: Tests learning with synthetic label noise on CIFAR and FASHION-MNIST using several loss functions, extending the noisy-label setting beyond the random-label memorization claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites random-label memorization and Arpit et al.'s learning-dynamics finding as prior work; those cited results are not rows. Its own noisy-label experiments report test accuracy across corruption rates and describe training dynamics, but do not report training error on random labels or chance-level test error for fully random labels.
record.test_reason: The study's own CIFAR-10 learning trajectories test V6: with CCE, predictive patterns emerge before strong fitting of noisy labels. It does not establish perfect training-set fitting under random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose Lq and truncated Lq losses and conclude that experiments verify noise robustness under closed-set and open-set noise. Their dynamics experiments show that increasing q can delay overfitting, while excessively large q can hinder optimization and classification accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses synthetic label corruption and alternative loss functions on image-classification datasets; it does not reproduce the original random-label intervention or its training-error and chance-test-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise rate and loss parameter q affect overfitting and classification accuracy; the text reports larger q thresholds as data become noisier, while too-large q can reduce accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Lq with q = 0.7 produces smaller softmax values for incorrectly labeled training samples than CCE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the loss can reduce noisy-label fitting in partially corrupted training data.

record.problems: For the claim versions here, the paper does not report training error under random labels; its learning-dynamics results are qualitative figure descriptions, and the reported noisy-label test accuracies do not establish the all-random-label endpoint.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports many test-accuracy cells across three datasets, six loss functions and multiple uniform and class-dependent noise rates. These do not measure training error, and the study does not report the all-random-label endpoint; they were therefore not extracted as rows for V4. Table 2 likewise reports test accuracy for open-set and closed-set noise, without training error.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios for true versus random labels and convergence slowdown as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training-set fitting throughout the corruption sweep and the completely random-label endpoint. Table 1 reports test-accuracy degradation across intermediate noise rates, but cannot establish the combined memorization-and-generalization claim.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them impairs true-label generalization.
Completely random-label training and generality of the learning sequence across other datasets and architectures.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Table 1's test-accuracy results and Table 2's method comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out. Neither supplies the training-error measurements needed to establish V4's joint claim. Reduced or prevented overfitting under a deliberately noise-robust loss does not by itself challenge V6's ordering.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on completely random labels or report training error and test error at chance for that setting.
Does not compare training time for random versus true labels or quantify convergence against the fraction of corrupted labels.
Does not use shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Tests synthetic label-noise rates and reports test accuracy, but does not report training error across the rates or test the all-random-label endpoint required by the version.
Does not test whether regularization or augmentation prevents fitting random labels or whether removing them harms generalization on true labels.
Tests dynamics under uniform label noise on CIFAR-10 with CCE and Lq losses; does not test completely random labels or establish the sequence across other datasets and architectures.

rows.subject: ResNet-34
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average softmax outputs for correctly and wrongly labeled training samples during training.
rows.measure: Average softmax prediction for correctly and wrongly labeled training samples over training.
rows.value: For wrongly labeled samples, average softmax remained small at the beginning and grew quickly when the model started overfitting.
rows.note: Qualitative description in the text; no numerical figure values are given.
rows.check: The reported early suppression and later rapid increase of predictions for incorrect training labels supports the claimed sequence. Qualitative reporting alone does not make the effect partial. Specify that softmax values concern the provided training label.

rows.subject: ResNet-34
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average softmax outputs for correctly and wrongly labeled training samples during training.
rows.measure: Average softmax prediction for correctly and wrongly labeled training samples over training.
rows.value: Lq loss resulted in significantly smaller softmax values for wrongly labeled data.
rows.note: Qualitative description in the text; no numerical figure values are given.
rows.check: Smaller softmax values for incorrect labels under Lq than CCE measure reduced noisy-label fitting, but this comparison alone does not establish whether real patterns were learned before noise.

rows.subject: ResNet-34
rows.operation_detail: Compared test-accuracy and validation-loss trajectories during training with Lq loss at different q values.

conditions.value: CCE at q = 0; higher q values

rows.measure: Training dynamics and overfitting over epochs.
rows.value: With CCE, the classifier first learned predictive patterns, presumably from noise-free labels, before overfitting strongly to noisy labels; increasing q delayed overfitting and attained higher classification accuracies.
rows.note: Text describes the trajectory qualitatively; individual curve values are not stated.
rows.check: The CCE trajectory explicitly shows early predictive-pattern learning followed by noisy-label overfitting. Separate this finding from the higher-q mitigation comparison; delayed overfitting alone does not establish the full sequence.

relationships.condition: ResNet-34 trained with default Adam and CCE on CIFAR-10 with uniform label noise.
relationships.reason: R1 reports initially small predictions for incorrect labels followed by rapid growth; R3 reports predictive-pattern learning before strong noisy-label overfitting at noise rates 0.2 and 0.6. Attribution of early patterns specifically to clean labels remains the authors' interpretation.
relationships.display_finding: Incorrect-label prediction probabilities were initially small before growing rapidly, with predictive-pattern learning preceding strong overfitting at noise rates 0.2 and 0.6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10, ResNet-34, uniform label noise, tested loss settings
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe early predictive-pattern learning before strong noisy-label overfitting with CCE and report delayed overfitting with higher q; this is partial evidence for the claimed sequence (R1–R3).
